verdicts.title: Open issue #880 is materially wider than its title: 87 CUDA-requiring tests across 13 files in 5 packages carry a skipif but no `cuda` marker, so they run in no CI lane
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. (1) The marker contract holds: conftest.py:36-42 turns `pytest.mark.cuda` into a runtime skip, .github/workflows/pr.yml:71/145/160/177 and ci.yml select `not cuda ...` on CPU lanes and `cuda and not slow` / `cuda` on the three GPU lanes, so a bare `skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available())` without the marker is selected-then-skipped on CPU and deselected on GPU. (2) I re-ran my own AST walk (module pytestmark + class + function decorators) over packages/ and tests/ and got exactly the finding's 13 files with exactly its per-file counts summing to 87 (plus 6 more in opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_device_resolution.py that the finding conservatively excluded, so 93 by my count). (3) Measured collection matches the evidence verbatim: test_autocast.py 26 on CPU / 0 under -m cuda; test_vmap_autocast_bf16.py 5 / 0; opaque-engine/tests/profiling/test_memory.py 16 / 0; opaque-dpsgd/tests/functional/test_compile.py 11 / 0; kernels/test_compile.py 4 / 0; test_batchify.py 3 / 0; test_precision_training.py 8 / 0. test_lora.py (12/51) and test_linear_cross_entropy.py (2/46) still collect a little on CUDA only because individual tests grew an explicit @pytest.mark.cuda; their module pytestmark at test_lora.py:44 and test_linear_cross_entropy.py:38 is still the bare scalar skipif, i.e. #880 is unfixed. (4) The empty-leg consequence holds: python-tests.yml runs run_python_test_package.sh once per suite path, and packages/opaque-base, opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing and opaque-alignment collect 0 under -m cuda, so with allow-empty-test-selection: true those paths exit 5 and are converted to success. (5) The delta claim is exact: git diff --stat 4b13d82..12146ec4 over the five touched files is 720 insertions / 65 deletions, and no delta commit added a marker. Severity kept at medium to match the repo's own label on #880; no privacy or runtime behavior is affected, but the fused-kernel and autocast GPU surface has no executing coverage on any lane. Substantially duplicates OPEN #880, whose body already describes the same defect class for 44 of the functions, so filed as known with widened scope (38 more functions in 11 more files, including whole files in opaque-alignment, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd and opaque-transformers).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: At HEAD, 87 CUDA-requiring test functions in 13 files across opaque-alignment, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-engine, opaque-patches and opaque-transformers use `skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available())` with no `pytest.mark.cuda`. Every CPU lane selects them and skips them at runtime; every CUDA lane deselects them (measured: 0 collected under `-m cuda` for test_autocast.py, test_vmap_autocast_bf16.py, profiling/test_memory.py, dpsgd functional/test_compile.py, kernels/test_compile.py, test_batchify.py, test_precision_training.py). So a regression in bf16-autocast per-sample gradients through the fused kernels, or in CUDA memory-stat reporting, or in CUDA torch.compile parity, ships with a green CUDA gate. No privacy guarantee and no shipped runtime behavior changes; the impact is purely absent GPU regression coverage. Open #880 already tracks the two largest files (44 functions); the remaining 38 functions in 11 files are outside its stated scope.

verdicts.title: OPQ-381 was closed (#836) without a change: exit-5 is still converted to success and two of five distributed-lane legs plus the foundation leg of every CUDA lane still pass on zero tests
verdicts.reasoning: Facts verified individually. .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:43-46 still reads `if [[ "$status" -eq 5 && "$ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION" == "true" ]]; then echo ::notice ...; exit 0`. `allow-empty-test-selection: true` is still set at ci.yml:41,100,112,126 and pr.yml:81,145,160,177 (also prepare-release-implementation.yml:314,398,415,434) - i.e. the distributed lane and all three CUDA lanes. git log 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- that script returns only 039fc012 (#876, the CUDA preflight). My own collection run under the distributed lane's exact marker reproduces the evidence table exactly: opaque-base 0, opaque-accounting 0, opaque-auditing 0, opaque-patches 0, tests 0, opaque-dpsgd 6, opaque-dpftrl 5, opaque-engine 10, opaque-optimizers 2, opaque-alignment 1, opaque-transformers 10; since python-tests.yml:164-176 invokes the runner once per suite path, the Foundation leg (base+accounting+auditing) and the Integration leg (tests) both select nothing and are converted to success. Under -m cuda the foundation trio and opaque-alignment also collect 0. tests/integration/ddp/test_dpsgd_sampler_short_run_parity.py:37 and the dpftrl twin are still `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.slow, pytest.mark.cuda]`, which is why the root tests/ tree selects nothing on the distributed lane. ci.yml:199-213 does make publish-dev-wheels depend on those job results. Two corrections: (a) #836 was not merely 'closed without a change' by oversight - it was closed as not_planned on 2026-09-01 with no comment, i.e. deliberately declined, so this is a re-litigation of an accepted decision rather than a new discovery; (b) the claim 'nothing downstream reads TEST_RESULTS_FILE' is wrong - .github/actions/upload-python-coverage/action.yml:22-27 reads it to decide whether to produce and upload coverage (it just does not fail the job). Severity stays low: this is a latent fail-open that needs a second defect (a dropped or mistyped marker) to hide anything, and the distributed/CUDA lanes do select and run tests today on the legs that matter. Filed as known under the still-open umbrella #774 (its child #836 is the exact issue).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: At HEAD the runner still converts pytest exit 5 to success whenever ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION=true, which is set on the distributed lane and all three CUDA lanes in both pr.yml and ci.yml. Measured now: on `-m 'distributed and not cuda'` the Foundation suite (opaque-base+accounting+auditing) and the Integration suite (tests/) collect zero tests and report green having executed nothing; under `-m cuda` the same Foundation suite and the opaque-alignment path also collect zero. The live consequence is only informational - a green check that cannot distinguish 12 tests from 0. A real failure requires a second change that drops or mistypes the `distributed` or `cuda` marker; then that lane collects nothing everywhere and still gates publish-dev-wheels (ci.yml:199-213) green. Issue #836 asked for a MIN_TESTS floor and was closed as not_planned on 2026-09-01 with no code change and no recorded rationale.

verdicts.title: OPQ-386 was closed (#841) without a change: Python 3.12 still executes zero tests while all ten wheels advertise it
verdicts.reasoning: Every cited fact reproduced. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` returns nothing (exit 1). validate-distributions.yml:19 is `python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]`; python-tests.yml:34-38 defaults the python-version input to "3.11"; the only explicit pins anywhere in .github are 3.11 and 3.13 (ci.yml:56,117; pr.yml:96,109,165,182; prepare-release-implementation.yml:335,353,421,440; build-distributions.yml:37,129). All ten package pyprojects plus the root carry `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` and `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"`. No endpoints-only interpreter policy is documented: CONTRIBUTING.md:163 only says the dependency-selection lanes are minimum (3.11) / latest (3.13), docs/getting-started/installation.md:11 and docs/development/index.md:20 advertise 3.11 through 3.13, and AGENTS.md:326 notes 3.12 is the dev VM's default interpreter. Correction to framing: #841 was closed as not_planned on 2026-09-01 with no comment, so the gap is a declined issue rather than an unnoticed one. Severity low and firmly so: this is a metadata-vs-coverage mismatch with no privacy or correctness consequence, and 3.11/3.13 bracket nearly all interpreter-specific behavior. Filed as known under the still-open umbrella #774 (child #841 is the exact issue).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: All ten Opaque distributions declare `requires-python >=3.11,<3.14` and a `Python :: 3.12` classifier, while no CI lane anywhere in .github runs on 3.12 (grep finds no occurrence; the test workflow defaults to 3.11 and the only explicit pins are 3.11 and 3.13). A 3.12-only regression - a dependency resolving to a different wheel, or interpreter-specific torch.func/pytree behavior - would ship unflagged in a release whose metadata promises 3.12. Nothing here changes a privacy guarantee, and 3.11/3.13 bracket most such behavior, so the concrete exposure is a documentation/metadata promise CI never validates. #841 requested either one cheap 3.12 leg or dropping the classifier and was closed as not_planned with neither done.

verdicts.title: A shipped feature's only integration regression tests are gated behind a capability probe that turns the feature's removal into a silent skip
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is real and I verified each link: tests/integration/noise/test_auto_clipping_mf_noise.py:311-333 defines `_per_group_supported_by_mf_noise()` which returns False on `except TypeError as exc: if 'PerGroup' in str(exc)`, and :330-340 wires it into an autouse `_gate` fixture on `TestPerGroupAutoSxMf` that calls pytest.skip; `opaque.exceptions.InputTypeError` is `class InputTypeError(OpaqueError, TypeError)` (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:31), so an Opaque-native rejection naming PerGroup would indeed be swallowed as a skip. I ran the class: 12 tests pass today (2 methods x 6 strategies), so the probe currently returns True and the stale docstrings at :36 and :330-333 still tell the reader mf_gaussian_noise rejects PerGroup 'on plain main' pending PR #192, which has landed. Two corrections that gut the stated impact: (1) the finding's own cited raise sites do not produce the trigger - `_expect_clipped` (_engine.py:456-474) never mentions PerGroup in either message, and the only 'PerGroup' InputTypeError in _engine.py:143-149 fires on non-tensor leaves, which the probe's all-tensor template cannot hit; the fail-open therefore needs a hypothetical future rejection whose message happens to contain 'PerGroup'. (2) the removal of per-group MF noise support would NOT be invisible: packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py holds 22 ungated tests that call mf_gaussian_noise with PerGroup-clipped inputs across all six strategies (plus paired second-moment cases) and would hard-fail, as would per-group cases in test_second_moment_noise.py and test_mf_state_serialization.py. So what actually remains is a narrow test-hygiene defect - a fail-open gate plus stale pending-PR prose over 12 composition tests - not a blind spot for the feature. Downgraded accordingly; the fix is the trivial deletion the finding already sketches. Not tracked by any open issue.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: tests/integration/noise/test_auto_clipping_mf_noise.py still carries an autouse `_gate` fixture whose capability probe skips the 12 `TestPerGroupAutoSxMf` tests when mf_gaussian_noise raises a TypeError whose message contains 'PerGroup'. The feature shipped, the probe returns True, and all 12 pass today. If a future change re-rejected PerGroup bounds with an `InputTypeError` (a TypeError subclass) naming PerGroup, those 12 AUTO-S x per-group-MF composition tests would turn from FAIL into SKIP and that specific composition would go unguarded - but the loss of per-group MF support itself would still fail loudly, because packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py has 22 ungated tests driving mf_gaussian_noise with PerGroup bounds. Residual defect: a fail-open guard over 12 tests plus module and class docstrings that still describe PR #192 as unlanded.
verdicts._note: mechanism real, consequence overstated; downgraded to low
